title: Spirit-wrought holiness is true and God-pleasing
source_text: XIII. Et certe cum sanctitas & justitia illa quam in fidelibus format & efficit Spi-ritus Sanctus, sit, Apostolo docente, sanctitas & justitia veritatis, id est, sanctitas vera, germana & syncera, non simulata & hypocritica, & in ea sit quoddam imi-tamentum, & similitudo quaedam ipsius sanctitatis & justitiae divinae, fieri non potest quin Deo placeat & probetur, juxta illud Prophetae, Justus Dominus justitiam diligit; illum qui rectus est aspicit vultus ejus, Psal. 11. Quo respiciens Petrus, agno-scit in qualibet gente acceptum esse Deo quemvis, qui Deum timet & justitiam ope-ratur, Act. 10. 35.
pass_a_gloss: And certainly, since that holiness and righteousness which the Holy Spirit forms and effects in believers is, as the Apostle teaches, the holiness and righteousness of truth—that is, true, genuine, and sincere holiness, not simulated and hypocritical—and since in it there is a certain imitation and likeness of the divine holiness and righteousness itself, it cannot be but that it pleases and is approved by God, according to that of the Prophet: The Lord is righteous; he loves righteousness; his countenance beholds the upright (Psalm 11). Looking to which Peter acknowledges that in every nation whoever fears God and works righteousness is accepted with him (Acts 10:35).
pass_b_english: Spirit-formed holiness is true sanctity of truth—not hypocrisy—and bears a likeness to divine justice.
Therefore it pleases God; Peter: in every nation whoever fears God and works righteousness is accepted.

choices.why: Key lemma for De Justitia densify §1047.
